assertions: The shim execs the skill-manager it finds and hands the arguments over.
The shim does not resolve to itself when its own directory leads PATH.
The shim still refuses, with its diagnostic, when nothing is reachable.
The generated body contains no doubled percent.

evidence.graph: checkout-home node checkout.home.provisioned, three bounded invocations on a hermetic PATH: nothing reachable, a stub reachable, and the shim own directory first with the stub behind it
evidence.mutation: Restored `printf '%%s'` at BOTH sites in cliScript() (2 occurrences counted first; mutating one would have left the other half of the filter working). Killed three named tests: "the cli entrypoint body carries no unformatted percent" on the BYTES, and both "the cli entrypoint execs the skill-manager it finds on PATH" and "the cli entrypoint never resolves to itself" on the exec'd output -- each reporting the refusal banner where the stub sentinel was expected. Reverted; shasum -a 256 -c OK.
unit: LauncherShimsTest "the cli entrypoint execs the skill-manager it finds on PATH" -- on the stub CLI output and its view of the arguments
LauncherShimsTest "the cli entrypoint never resolves to itself" -- bounded, so recursion is a named failure
LauncherShimsTest "the cli entrypoint refuses when no skill-manager is reachable" -- on the diagnostic, not on a bare non-zero exit
LauncherShimsTest "the cli entrypoint body carries no unformatted percent"

ticket.found_by: an operator running the shim on a machine with a working CLI on PATH
ticket.objective: LauncherShims.cliScript() emitted `printf '%%s'`. That is correct in script(String), which ends in `.formatted(agent)`, and wrong here, where nothing unescapes it: the doubled percent reached bash literally, and bash `printf '%%s'` prints the two characters `%s` rather than its argument. So the filtered PATH became the single entry `%s`, `command -v skill-manager` found nothing, and the shim took the "no CLI is provisioned" branch UNCONDITIONALLY. Measured with /opt/homebrew/bin/skill-manager on PATH: exit 127. All seven onboarded constituent homes affected. It survived because CheckoutHomeProvisioned only ever exercised the no-CLI-reachable case -- SKILL_MANAGER_CLI cleared and PATH set to the shim's own directory -- and asserted a non-zero exit. A shim that ALWAYS exits 127 satisfies that perfectly. A one-sided assertion cannot tell a correct refusal from a dead command. Worse than under-tested: the PATH-filtering loop exists so the shim does not resolve to ITSELF (LaunchEnv puts <home>/bin/cli at the front of the launch PATH). With printf broken the filter had never once run, so the self-recursion guard was untested in practice.
ticket.resolution: Write the percent once, and say in the javadoc why it is once here and twice one method above -- naming the trap for whoever adds a format specifier later. The assertion is now two-sided in both the unit suite and the graph, asserted on the exec'd CLI's OUTPUT rather than on a zero exit (a shim that exits 0 without launching is the defect the shim exists to prevent), plus a direct assertion that no `%%` survives in the generated body. The recursion guard is exercised for real: the shim's own directory FIRST on PATH and a working stub behind it, exactly as a launch arranges them, with a bounded wait so a self-exec spin is a NAMED failure rather than a hung suite. Every case runs on a hermetic PATH holding links to bash, dirname and tr and nothing else -- emptying PATH makes the shim die on a missing dirname, which is a non-zero exit that looks like a refusal and is not one, and leaving /usr/bin on it would let the refusal case find a real skill-manager on some machines.
